About

I’ve spent more than eight years building tools at the meeting point of computer graphics, computer vision and machine learning.

My PhD at ÉTS Montréal focused on reconstructing, transferring and editing 3D surfaces, with industrial collaborations at Autodesk and Ubisoft. At Ubisoft I helped build FaceShifter, a production system for generating and editing 3D faces at scale. Today at SmileShape I design the geometry algorithms behind automated dental CAD, turning scanned anatomy into manufacturable dentures.

I enjoy the whole path: reading the paper, writing the C++ or Python, and making sure the tool actually helps the artist, designer or clinician using it.

Selected projects

Drag to rotate

Automated dentures

SmileShape, dental CAD

Geometry algorithms that turn a patient’s scan into a manufacturable denture: teeth placed along arch splines, a gum base built by constrained deformation, surface reconstruction and Boolean operations. Shown: a full upper and lower denture and its individual parts, designed by the pipeline. Three US patents pending.

SmileShape

3D faces at scale

Ubisoft, FaceShifter

Part-based morphable face models: edit one region, like the nose or jaw, and the rest of the face stays intact. Behind the FaceShifter pipeline for game characters. Best student paper, Graphics Interface 2020.

PaperVideoUbisoft article

Generative face textures

Ubisoft La Forge, machine learning

Artists pick skin, hair, eye and lip colours (and facial hair), and a deep generative model paints a matching high-resolution texture for the face mesh. Best student paper, MIG 2020; extended in Computers & Graphics 2021.

MIG 2020 paperComputers & Graphics 2021

Shape correspondence and animation transfer

Autodesk, PhD research

Matching points between very different 3D characters so skeletons, skin weights and other attributes move automatically from one to another. Shipped as a Maya plugin, now a granted US patent.

PaperPatentVideo

Interactive 3D visualization for multivariable calculus

Linköping University, MSc thesis (2013)

A set of interactive 3D tools, built in Java and OpenGL (JOGL), that let students explore partial derivatives, tangent planes, gradients, directional derivatives, critical points and Lagrange multipliers on any surface they type in. Includes a custom math expression parser, real-time mouse picking of a trace point on the surface, parametric surfaces, and contour plots linked between 2D and 3D views. Published for the Multivariable Calculus course at Linköping University.

Thesis PDF
